description: Experience the ultimate Middle Eastern feast with our whole slow roasted Lamb Ouzi, a dish renowned for its incredible tenderness and rich, aromatic spices. The lamb is lovingly cooked until fall-off-the-bone succulent, then served majestically over a bed of fragrant spiced rice, making it a truly unforgettable centerpiece for any special occasion. This traditional recipe captures the essence of Middle Eastern hospitality and culinary excellence.

instructions.title: Prepare the Lamb
instructions.text: Pat the lamb shoulder or leg dry with paper towels. Using a sharp knife, score the fatty side of the lamb deeply in a crosshatch pattern, being careful not to cut into the meat too much. This helps the marinade penetrate and fat render. In a small bowl, combine olive oil, salt, black pepper, seven spice blend, cinnamon, nutmeg, cardamom, and minced garlic to form a thick paste. Rub this spice paste all over the lamb, ensuring it gets into the scored areas.

instructions.title: Marinate and Sear (Optional)
instructions.text: Place the seasoned lamb in a large roasting pan. If time allows, cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight, to allow the flavors to meld. Before roasting, bring the lamb to room temperature for about 1 hour. For extra flavor and color, you can sear the lamb on all sides in a large, hot skillet with a little oil before transferring it to the roasting pan.

instructions.title: Slow Roasting Process
instructions.text: Preheat your oven to 160°C (325°F). Add the chopped onion and bay leaves to the roasting pan around the lamb. Pour 2 cups of water or broth into the bottom of the pan. Cover the roasting pan tightly with foil and roast for 3 to 4 hours, or until the lamb is fork-tender and easily pulls away from the bone. Baste occasionally with the pan juices. For the last 30 minutes, remove the foil to allow the lamb to brown and crisp slightly.

instructions.title: Prepare the Spiced Rice
instructions.text: While the lamb rests after roasting, prepare the spiced rice. In a large pot, melt 2 tablespoons of butter or olive oil. Saute 1 chopped onion until translucent. Add 1 tablespoon of seven spice blend, 1/2 teaspoon of cinnamon, and a pinch of cardamom. Stir for 1 minute until fragrant. Add the rinsed Basmati rice and stir to coat. Pour in 4 cups of lamb or chicken broth (or water), bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15-20 minutes until the liquid is absorbed and rice is fluffy.

instructions.title: Assemble the Ouzi Platter
instructions.text: Carefully transfer the whole roasted lamb to a large serving platter. The lamb should be tender enough to shred easily. Fluff the spiced rice with a fork and spread it generously around the base of the lamb on the platter. You can also shred some of the lamb and mix it directly into the rice for a more integrated presentation.

instructions.title: Garnish and Serve
instructions.text: Ladle some of the flavorful pan juices over the lamb and rice. Garnish generously with toasted pine nuts, toasted slivered almonds, and fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately with a side of yogurt or a simple cucumber salad for a complete and authentic Middle Eastern feast.

tips: For maximum flavor, ensure the lamb marinates for at least 4 hours, or ideally overnight, allowing the spices to deeply infuse the meat.

Roasting low and slow is key for tender, fall-off-the-bone lamb. Use a meat thermometer to ensure the internal temperature reaches 63°C (145°F) for medium-rare, or higher for more well-done, then allow it to rest.
Serve Lamb Ouzi with a vibrant fresh salad like fattoush or a simple cucumber and yogurt sauce to balance the rich flavors of the lamb and rice.
